title: Composition and base change for separation and finite presentation of algebraic spaces
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], and work with algebraic spaces over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space] in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention], with sheaf fibre products [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. A morphism is separated when its diagonal is a representable closed immersion, meaning all scheme tests of the diagonal are closed immersions [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Local finite presentation is tested on etale scheme charts [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. Finite presentation additionally requires quasi-compactness and quasi-separatedness. A space is quasi-compact if it admits a surjective etale scheme atlas with quasi-compact source [def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme]. A morphism $A\to B$ is quasi-compact if $A\times_BT$ is a quasi-compact space for every quasi-compact algebraic space $T$ mapping to $B$ [lem-sfb-space-quasicompact-fppf-local]. Quasi-separated means that the diagonal is quasi-compact. Let $f:X\to Y$ and $g:Y\to Z$ be morphisms of algebraic spaces over $S$. If both are separated, then $g\circ f$ is separated. If both are of finite presentation, then $g\circ f$ is of finite presentation. If both are locally of finite presentation, then $g\circ f$ is locally of finite presentation. For every morphism $Y'\to Y$, if $f$ is separated then $X\times_YY'\to Y'$ is separated. These assertions do not require that any of the morphisms be representable.

source.place: Tags 03KL (spaces-morphisms-lemma-base-change-separated), 03KQ (spaces-morphisms-lemma-composition-separated), and 03XQ (spaces-morphisms-lemma-composition-finite-presentation), including the locally finite presentation clause.

proof.text: Put $D=X\times_YX$ and $E=X\times_ZX$. Their sheaf fibre-product universal properties give $\Delta_{X/Z}=j\circ\Delta_{X/Y}$, where $j:D\to E$ is the pullback of $\Delta_{Y/Z}:Y\to Y\times_ZY$ along $(f,f):E\to Y\times_ZY$. Indeed, a section of the pullback is a pair $(x_1,x_2)$ together with a common value $y=f(x_1)=f(x_2)$, exactly a section of $D$. For $X\prime=X\times_YY\prime$ the same section calculation identifies $\Delta_{X\prime/Y\prime}$ with the pullback of $\Delta_{X/Y}$ along $X\prime\times_{Y\prime}X\prime\to D$. These identifications are natural in every test scheme, so they are identities of the indicated sheaf fibre products.

source.place: Tags 03KL (lemma-base-change-separated) and 03KQ (lemma-composition-separated): diagonal pullback and factorization

proof.text: A pullback of a representable closed immersion $i:A\to B$ along any algebraic space $C\to B$ is again a representable closed immersion: for a scheme $T\to C$, its test is $T\times_BA\to T$, one of the scheme tests in the hypothesis on $i$. Two representable closed immersions $A\to B\to C$ compose: for a scheme $T\to C$, first $B_T\to T$ is a closed immersion of schemes and then $A_T\to B_T$ is one, so their composite is a closed immersion by the cited scheme composition lemma. Apply these two observations to the diagonal identities of step 1. If $f,g$ are separated, both factors of $\Delta_{X/Z}$ are representable closed immersions. If $f$ is separated, the base-changed diagonal is one as well. This proves both separatedness assertions without representability of $f$ or $g$.

source.place: Tags 03KL and 03KQ, using representable scheme tests; scheme composition: morphisms.tex Tag 01QS (lemma-composition-closed-immersion)

proof.text: Use the stated all-test definition of quasi-compactness. If $a:A\to B$ and $b:B\to C$ are quasi-compact and $T\to C$ is a quasi-compact space, then $B_T$ is quasi-compact and $A\times_BB_T\cong A\times_CT$ is quasi-compact. Thus quasi-compact morphisms compose. A base change is quasi-compact by the cited base-change statement. Consequently, when $f,g$ are quasi-separated, $\Delta_f$ and $\Delta_g$ are quasi-compact, the map $j$ of step 1 is quasi-compact as a pullback of $\Delta_g$, and $j\Delta_f=\Delta_{gf}$ is quasi-compact by the just-proved composition argument. Thus $gf$ is quasi-separated.

source.place: Tag 03HG (lemma-composition-quasi-compact), omitted transitivity argument written out; Tag 03KQ, quasi-separated clause

proof.text: Let $P$ be local finite presentation of scheme morphisms. The scheme etale-locality node says that $P$ is etale local on source-and-target. Apply the presentation criterion to $g$: choose schemes $V,W$, representable etale maps $b:V\to Y$ (surjective), $c:W\to Z$, and a map $k:V\to W$ with $gb=ck$. If $g$ is locally of finite presentation, $k$ has $P$. Form the algebraic space $X_V=X\times_YV$ and choose a representable surjective etale scheme atlas $a:U\to X_V$. The composite $d:U\to X$ is representable surjective etale: on a scheme test $T\to X$ its intermediate scheme is $T\times_YV$, etale and surjective over $T$ by the definition of $b$; the pullback of $a$ is etale and surjective over this scheme. The cited scheme covering-composition lemma proves the assertion for the composite test. Let $h:U\to V$ be the other projection. The square $fd=bh$ is a presentation diagram for $f$, so if $f$ is locally of finite presentation, $h$ has $P$.

source.place: Tag 03XQ (lemma-composition-finite-presentation), expanded remark-composition-P using Tag 03MJ (lemma-local-source-target); topologies.tex Tag 0217 for composite scheme covers

proof.text: Under the locally finite presentation hypotheses on $f,g$, step 4 gives scheme maps $U\xrightarrow{h}V\xrightarrow{k}W$ locally of finite presentation. Their composite $kh$ is locally of finite presentation by the scheme composition lemma. The equality $(gf)d=c(kh)$, with $d$ surjective etale and $c$ etale, is a presentation diagram for $gf$. The presentation criterion, applicable by scheme etale locality of local finite presentation, therefore proves that $gf$ is locally of finite presentation.

source.place: Tag 03XQ, locally finite presentation clause; morphisms.tex Tag 01TR (lemma-composition-finite-presentation)

proof.text: If $f,g$ are of finite presentation, each is locally of finite presentation, quasi-compact and quasi-separated by the stated definition. Step 5 gives local finite presentation of $gf$; step 3 gives its quasi-compactness and quasi-separatedness. These three properties are exactly finite presentation. All chart refinements above were representable etale maps from schemes, while $f,g$ and the base-change map were arbitrary morphisms of algebraic spaces.

lean.statement: theorem separated_finitePresentation_composition_and_separated_baseChange {S : Scheme.{u}} {X Y Z : AlgebraicSpace S} (f : X ⟶ Y) (g : Y ⟶ Z) : (IsSeparatedPresheafMap f.hom.hom → IsSeparatedPresheafMap g.hom.hom → IsSeparatedPresheafMap (f ≫ g).hom.hom) ∧ ((MapIsLocallyOfFinitePresentation f ∧ IsQuasiCompactPresheafMap f.hom.hom ∧ IsQuasiCompactPresheafMap (diagonalPresheafMap f.hom.hom)) → (MapIsLocallyOfFinitePresentation g ∧ IsQuasiCompactPresheafMap g.hom.hom ∧ IsQuasiCompactPresheafMap (diagonalPresheafMap g.hom.hom)) → (MapIsLocallyOfFinitePresentation (f ≫ g) ∧ IsQuasiCompactPresheafMap (f ≫ g).hom.hom ∧ IsQuasiCompactPresheafMap (diagonalPresheafMap (f ≫ g).hom.hom))) ∧ (MapIsLocallyOfFinitePresentation f → MapIsLocallyOfFinitePresentation g → MapIsLocallyOfFinitePresentation (f ≫ g)) ∧ (∀ (Y' : AlgebraicSpace S) (h : Y' ⟶ Y), IsSeparatedPresheafMap f.hom.hom → IsSeparatedPresheafMap (Limits.pullback.snd f.hom.hom h.hom.hom))
lean.note: The conjunction renders the four independent implications. Finite presentation is expanded as the existing chartwise local finite presentation and atlas quasi-compactness predicates for the map and its diagonal. No representability hypothesis on f, g or the base change is imposed.
